tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file OR list a directory in the workspace (path relative to the workspace root). A directory returns its entry listing (subdirectories end with '/'). For a file, prefer the line-range form: pass offset (1-based start line) and limit (line count) to read only the slice you need — output is line-numbered and ends with a "(showing lines X-Y of N; use offset=Y+1 to continue)" hint when more remains. A range larger than the read budget returns an error; narrow the limit or use grep. Without offset/limit the whole file is read and truncated at max_chars (default $config.read_max_chars) with a "use offset=N to continue" hint — never re-read a file from the top, continue with that offset instead. Only read files relevant to the task; content-creation tasks do not need to explore the workspace.

path.description: file path OR directory path, relative to the workspace root

offset.description: 1-based start line for a line-range read

limit.description: max lines to read when offset is given

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search files in the workspace for a regex pattern. Use this to locate code before reading files — it is cheaper than reading whole files or running grep in the shell. pattern is a Python-style regex (e.g. "def build_\w+", "TODOs?"). path limits the search to a subdirectory or file (default: whole workspace); include filters by filename glob (e.g. "*.py", "*.md"). Hidden files and binary files are skipped. Output is capped at 100 hits as "path:  Line N: text"; narrow the pattern or path if the result is truncated. Workspace-relative paths returned here can be passed straight to read_file.

path.description: subdirectory or file to search (default: whole workspace)

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create or overwrite a file in the workspace. path is relative to the workspace root. This is the only way to create/modify code files: whole-file rewrite, do not edit files any other way.

path.description: file path, relative to the workspace root

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Edit an existing file by replacing one exact occurrence of old_string with new_string (path relative to the workspace root). Use this to MODIFY existing code — a targeted edit costs a few hundred tokens instead of re-emitting the whole file, keeps the context small, and never risks truncating the file. old_string must appear exactly once in the file; if it is missing or ambiguous the tool errors and asks for more context — include surrounding lines to make it unique. The result shows a unified diff. For NEW files use write_file.

path.description: file path, relative to the workspace root

old_string.description: exact text to replace (must appear exactly once)
